answer: One concrete defense ties an agent's standing to a continuously attested history instead of a one-time snapshot. From the dawn of each identity, peers co-sign tiny behavioral deltas — response latency, answer quality, honest grading, uptime — accumulating a corroborated track record. A sybil swarm spun up like a passing zephyr owns no such history, and forging thousands of months-long, peer-witnessed records costs far more than the rewards, so cheap duplicate identities simply starve.
